checks.claim: NG13: plane covariance is homogeneous with degree 3/2 for every Borel set by direct change of variables
checks.reason: On the plane-support measure Γ(dy,dz)=(2π)^-1|y|^-1/2 dy δ0(dz), scaling a Borel set A (whose z-coordinate on the support remains 0) gives Γ(rA)=∫_{rA}|y|^-1/2dy/(2π)=r^{2-1/2}Γ(A)=r^{3/2}Γ(A); the substitution is direct in the defining integral and not inferred from centered-ball masses.

checks.claim: NG13: planar Riesz factor, Dirac factor and their product are positive definite, Radon, tempered and spectral-admissible
checks.reason: |y|^-1/2 in R^2 has a positive Gaussian-mixture representation and is locally integrable; δ0(dz) is positive definite; the product quadratic form restricts the normal coordinates to coincide, leaving an integral of nonnegative planar quadratic forms. Finite mass proportional to R^{3/2} on balls gives polynomial growth/temperedness, and Bochner-Schwartz provides the positive tempered Radon spectral measure with α0+α=1/4+3/2<2.

checks.claim: NG13: vague convergence plus a bound C_n|x|^-3/2 forces C_n→∞
checks.reason: A bounded subsequence C_n≤C gives, for every nonnegative compactly supported continuous f, ∫f dΓ=lim∫f dΓ_n≤C∫f|x|^-3/2dx; by monotone-class/regularity extension Γ would be absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on R^3. But the annulus {1≤|y|≤2,z=0} has positive Γ mass and zero Lebesgue measure. Hence no bounded subsequence exists.

checks.claim: NG13: the envelope obstruction is scoped to a uniform scalar isotropic density envelope, not a counterexample to the stochastic equation
checks.reason: The text explicitly states it rules out only the uniform scalar isotropic density envelope used with an angular supremum, and labels the reopening condition as a uniform estimate without angular supremum or a singular-support-adapted comparison; no numerical inference against the stochastic equation is claimed.

checks.claim: NG16: J_c scaling and domains, finite positive J1
checks.reason: A>0, c>0, 0<r<2 are declared before the scaling. H=c^{1/(2-r)}K multiplies both terms by c^{2/(2-r)}, so J_c=c^{2/(2-r)}J_1. J1 is positive for small H and finite because r<2.

checks.claim: NG16: strict surrogate comparison 2J1<J2
checks.reason: Multiplying J1's objective by two gives sup{2AH^r-H^2}=2J1, and J2=2^{2/(2-r)}J1 with 2/(2-r)>1 because r>0; since J1>0 the strict inequality holds.

checks.claim: NG16: exact Gaussian tilted mean recovery and lost logarithmic factor for the deterministic surrogate
checks.reason: Under Q_h, E_{Q_h}Y=e^{σ²/2+σh}; Cauchy-Schwarz with E L_h²=e^{h²} gives E Y²≥e^{σ²+2σh-h²}, maximized at h=σ to e^{2σ²}=E Y². Replacing the tilted mean by e^{σh} gives max_h e^{2σh-h²}=e^{σ²}, losing the factor e^{σ²} in the original scale (σ² instead of 2σ² in the logarithm).

checks.claim: NG16: scope is generic scalar score arithmetic, not an SPDE no-go
checks.reason: The scope paragraph identifies the lost term and states that a deterministic surrogate needs an explicit negligible-error estimate; no stochastic-solution counterexample is asserted.

checks.claim: NG18: exact actual wave transform and its three q-region evaluation
checks.reason: The spatial reduction ∫G_uG_vG_wG_z gives area derivative 2(R-max(C,|q|))_+, leading to I as the iterated integral; the q<0, 0≤q≤t, q≥t contributions are stated and their sum equals I=[2b²+4bc+2c²-c+1]/[8bc(b+1)(2b+1)(b+c-1)(2b+2c-1)]. Consistency checks hold: at c=1 this reduces to (b+1)/[4b²(2b+1)²].

checks.claim: NG18: convolution operands, S≤1, nonnegative parameters and bridge identity including endpoints
checks.reason: The convolution of e^{-s|q|} with e^{-A|q|} evaluated at w equals 2S_{A,s}(w)/(s+A), with S=e^{-Aw}+A∫_0^w e^{-At}e^{-s(w-t)}dt≥0 and S≤1 by bounding e^{-s(w-t)}≤1. η≥0 and τ=s-1/2≥0, so b=1+ν>0 and p=√(b²+2η)>0. The bridge integral ∫_0^1[b²+2ηt+2τt(1-t)]^{-3/2}dt equals 2(p+b)/[bp((p+b)²+2τ)] (verified by the quadratic completion; at η=τ=0 both sides are b^{-3}).

checks.claim: NG18: M_b resolvent partial-fraction identity and exact fractions at the test point
checks.reason: The positive-rate triple-resolvent formula ∫_0^∞[(z²+q1²)(z²+q2²)(z²+q3²)]^{-1}dz=π(q1+q2+q3)/[2q1q2q3(q1+q2)(q2+q3)(q3+q1)] yields M_b(η;A)=(1+c+p+b)/[4bpc(c+1)(c+p+b)(1+p+b)]. At b=1, c=11/10, p=1, A=21/200 this is 1025/21483, and I=545/11616, so I-M=-6005/7562016<0, matching the stated fractions exactly.

checks.claim: NG18: limited scope of the oversized envelope
checks.reason: The no-go targets only the shift-erased bound M_b(0;A) and explicitly does not refute J≤I or an integrated comparison; ν=0 is a legitimate fixed-parameter value, continuity gives overshoot for some ν>0 nearby, and the surviving envelope retains S_{A,1/2}(w). No counterexample to the stochastic comparison J≤I is claimed.

checks.claim: NG19: admissible one-dimensional parent, legal indicator test, and 0<V<∞ before normalizing
checks.reason: d=1, α=1/2, a=99/100 satisfy α+a<2; the power kernels are positive definite by Gaussian mixtures and locally integrable. The indicator ψ=1_[0,1]×1_[-1,1] has finite double integral E_φ=16√2/3 and V=2E_φ/(2-a)=3200√2/303, which is finite and strictly positive, so Z=W(ψ)/√V is well defined.

checks.claim: NG19: distributional covariance profile m and rank-one projection P with PSD residual, no pointwise W(s,x)
checks.reason: m=(1/√V)∫C dy dr is locally integrable, Fubini identifies ⟨m,f⟩=E[W(f)Z] for smooth compactly supported tests, and m=B_a(s)F(x)/√V is bounded and nonnegative with m(s,x)m(t,y)≥8/V on the backward cone. The projection W=Zm+W^⊥ realizes P=m⊗m; C-P is Loewner positive by Cauchy-Schwarz, and the text correctly avoids any pointwise random field evaluation W(s,x).

checks.claim: NG19: exact coefficient bounds A_C<1/96 and A_P>1/48
checks.reason: For α=1/2, a=99/100, spatial integration gives the temporal integrand (t-s)^{1-α-a} and A_C=(1-a)/[(1-α)(2-α-a)(3-α-a)(4-α-a)]=20000/1932951<1/96. The terminal cone lies in {|x|<1-s,|y|<1-t}, where m(s,z)m(t,y)≥8/V, and the D=1 integral is 1/24, so A_P≥8/(24V)=101/(3200√2)>1/48.

checks.claim: NG19: full small-coupling mean comparison with O(h^4) remainder for parent and bounded profile
checks.reason: For the parent, amplified covariance r²C plus nonnegative mixed moments give ||X_n||_2≤√B_r r^{-n} and an L² tail O((|h|/r)^4); odd terms vanish by Gaussian symmetry. For P=Zm the deterministic Picard coefficients are bounded by M^n/(2n)! and the absolute mean series is dominated by E cosh(√(M|Z|))<∞, giving E u_C(h)=1+h²A_C+O(h^4) and E u_P(h)=1+h²A_P+O(h^4). The strict coefficient gap proves the small-h inequality.

checks.claim: NG19: equivalent-law tilt Q=C+(q-1)P and L_q moments, with A_Q<qA_P-1/96
checks.reason: L_q=q^{-1/2}e^{(1-q^{-1})Z²/2} has E L_q=1 and E L_q²=[q(2-q)]^{-1/2} for 1<q<2, and the tilted Gaussian covariance is C+(q-1)P. Linearity gives A_Q=A_C+(q-1)A_P, and A_P-A_C>1/96 implies A_Q<qA_P-1/96. The same measurable solution carries the O(h^4) L¹ remainder via Cauchy-Schwarz, and the note omits any stationary-model existence claim for Q.

checks.claim: NG33: shear matrix contraction failure and whole-space low-frequency witness
checks.reason: For t>0 the unit vector (0,1) maps to (t,1) with norm √(1+t²)>1. The symbol of J0S(t)J0^{-1} on E=H^{1/2}×H^{-1/2} is [[cos(tr),⟨ξ⟩sin(tr)/r],[-r sin(tr)/⟨ξ⟩,cos(tr)]], which tends to S0(t) as r↓0; normalized bumps in the second coordinate of J0z, supported on balls shrinking to zero, give image norms tending to √(1+t²), so S(t) is not a contraction on E.

checks.claim: NG33: Hölder-factor identity error and its counterexample
checks.reason: The claim x^n/(n!)^θ=A_nB_n is false; the correct weighted product is A_n^θ B_n^{1-θ}, as used in Proposition P:static-phase-all-orders. At θ=3/4, n=1, x=1 the weighted product is 2^{3/4}·(1/8)^{1/4}=1, whereas A_1B_1=2·(1/8)=1/4.

checks.claim: NG33: factorial denominator inference failure and valid weakening
checks.reason: With the permitted α=1 and k=3, k!k^{(2-α)k}=6·3^3=162<216=(k!)^3, so M/162 does not imply M/216 for M>0. The valid bound is k!k^{(2-α)k}≥(k!)^{3-α} via k!≤k^k, which at this example gives (3!)^2=36≤162; the scope paragraph correctly restricts the refutation to the numerical inference, not the actual coefficient bound.

limitations: NG18's analytic identifications (wave transform, bridge/resolvent, survival envelope) and NG19's tail/fixed-order machinery are checked against the supplied MiddleCross and Projection contexts, which are treated as explicit interfaces (accepted prior analyses, P:mixed, parent construction) rather than re-certified here.

The NG19 display writes the pair of one-dimensional pair integrations as ∫ over R² for (z,y); this is consistent notation for the two scalar integrations, and all checked computations were performed in d=1.
